title: swarm:rollback:v1
description:
One RollbackReceipt, published as a NIP-10 reply to the swarm:lease:v1 card it closes.

THE ONLY CARD THAT CAN REACH TIER 1 TODAY. RollbackReceipt.governance_attestation (crates/swarm-response/src/rollback.rs:263-285) holds a serialized ConsensusGovernanceReceipt over this receipt's canonical form WITH THAT FIELD CLEARED, and verify_release_attestation (crates/swarm-runtime/src/containment.rs:235-269) checks the signature AND the subject binding. It is actually called, at crates/swarm-runtime-http/src/http/containment.rs:219-222, inside containment_lease_release_handler in swarm_detect --serve.

None does NOT mean 'attested and fine'. Under a partition contingency it is UNATTESTED - BY DESIGN; otherwise it is UNATTESTED. Both refusals are correct; only the explanation differs, and the explanation is what the operator acts on.

issuer.description: WHO PRODUCED THE FACT. See the envelope's `issuer` for who published it.

emitted_at_ms.description: The RuntimeEvent's own emitted_at_ms, carried through unchanged. THE SORT KEY for every Perch surface. The Nostr event's `created_at` is a transport timestamp stamped at publish, because MAX_TIMESTAMP_DRIFT_SECS is 900 and REJECTS (crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs:2224-2231) and `created_at` is inside the Nostr signature, so a spooled card carrying its true emit time becomes permanently unpublishable fifteen minutes after it was produced.

lease_card_id.description: Nostr event id of the swarm:lease:v1 card. Also the `e` tag.

governance_attestation.description: OPAQUE. A serialized swarm_consensus::ConsensusGovernanceReceipt, or absent. swarm-response never reads it and neither does this schema; verify_release_attestation is the only code allowed to decide whether it is valid. `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` is what excludes it from its own signing subject for free.

rollback_receipt.x-carried-note: This object is a domain type carried VERBATIM. The Rust wire crate names the type rather than redeclaring its fields, so a field added upstream reaches the wire with no edit and a field removed upstream is a compile error. tools/check-perch-wire-parity.sh skips its property names on the Rust side for exactly that reason, and the golden vectors plus this schema are what hold the shape.

release_response.description: ContainmentReleaseResponse minus its receipt and schema_version (crates/swarm-runtime-http/src/http/containment.rs:126-145). PRESENT ONLY for trigger=manual: an expiry-triggered rollback comes from the TTL sweep with no HTTP request and therefore no such body. lease_closed FALSE on an HTTP 200 means release_lease attempted the inverse, it failed, and the lease was deliberately kept open for the next sweep — a host is still contained. INV-05 forbids reading the status code instead.

partition_state_at_execution.description: Which of the two UNATTESTED renderings applies (INV-08). `partitioned` or `healing` means UNATTESTED - BY DESIGN. Null means the console could not establish it and must say so rather than assume healthy.
